issue_context.title: In contrast to StartUnit() the StartTransientUnit() D-Bus call doesn't pass unit name metadata to PolicyKit authorization request
comments:
i don't understand what this bug report is precisely about?

That we don't send much details along with the polkit auth request for `org.freedesktop.systemd1.manage-units`? That's true, noone who looked into this sent us a patch for that yet. Happy to take a patch, if this is a feature request for that.

or what is this precisely about? I find this report puzzling, please elaborate?

There is stuff to reproduce problem.
Though it seems idea of problem should be enough.

testecho.c

```c
#include <unistd.h>
#include <stdio.h>
int main(int argc , char * argv [] ) {
 printf("%s",arv[1]);
}
```

```
gcc -g testecho.c -o testecho
```

example of service file
```
testecho@.service
[Unit]
Description='test echo'

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=testecho start %i
ExecStop=true

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

suppose user testecho in group testecho.

```
cat /etc/polkit-1/rules.d/10-testecho.rules
polkit.addRule(function(action, subject) {
if (action.id == "org.freedesktop.systemd1.manage-units" ) {
polkit.log("action lookup unit=" + action.lookup("unit") );
// !!! system-run action.lookup("unit") undefined
if ( action.lookup("unit") == "testechorun.scope" && subject.isInGroup("testecho") ) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
}
// ok systemctl start|stop isccache@ for /etc/systemd/system/isccache@.service
// purpose not root might start isc cache service if user memeber of cachemgr group
if ( RegExp("testecho@[A-Za-z0-9_-]+.service").test(action.lookup("unit")) && subject.isInGroup("testecho") ) {
return polkit.Result.YES;
}

}
});
```

if user testecho does
```
systemctl start testecho@aaa
```
then it is ok
but if run
```
systemd-run --scope -u techoechorun testecho aaa
```
then it fails.

problem is that for case 
```
systemctl start testecho@aaa
```
polkit jscript has  action.lookup("unit") expected value
but for case
```
systemd-run --scope -u techoechorun testecho aaa
```
action.lookup("unit") is undefined.

_In contrast to StartUnit() the StartTransientUnit() D-Bus call doesn't pass unit name metadata to PolicyKit authorization _request.__
This is core of the issue. Why? There is reason for this or just one is missed to do?
man systemd-run
_If a command is run as transient service unit, it will be started and managed by the service manager like any other service ...
 If a command is run as transient scope unit, it will be executed by systemd-run itself as parent process and will thus inherit the execution environment of the
 caller. **However, the processes of the command are managed by the service manager similar to normal services**, and will show up in the output of systemctl
 list-units. Execution in this case is synchronous, and will return only when the command finishes. This mode is enabled via the --scope switch (see below)._

--unit=Use this unit name instead of an automatically generated one.
If unit name is pointed why not to transfer it?
What is needed to progress this?

I think these really should be cleaned up if this is touched, i.e. move to the same place and be wrappers of each other?
